concerns.location: plan.md: Execution Plan Phase 2 / research.md: Statistical Methodology
concerns.text: No detrending or non-stationarity handling is planned. Over 1998–2020 both solar-wind parameters and Kp/Dst share solar-cycle-scale trends; full-series correlations can be inflated by common low-frequency variation, not just hourly coupling. The plan should at least report, e.g., correlations on first-differenced or 27-day-running-mean-detrended series as a sensitivity check, or explicitly justify why the raw-level association is the target construct.

concerns.location: plan.md: Phase 2 — 'raw p-values from the t-distribution with df = N_eff − 2'
concerns.text: It is unstated whether the N_eff/df adjustment applies to Spearman ρ as well as Pearson r. Applying the Pearson t-statistic formula to Spearman ρ is a common but non-standard approximation. State explicitly how p_raw is computed for Spearman (e.g., same t approximation on ρ, or rank-transformed Pearson with N_eff).

Stale contract still specifies 'adjusted for effective degrees of freedom (EDF) using Thomson's MTM' and 'Holm-Bonferroni-corrected p-value' — the exact un-spec'd elaborations the re-plan note says were reverted. This contract contradicts the plan's Pyper & Peterman + plain Bonferroni methodology and must be updated or removed so the implemented statistics match the validated schema.

Lag-1 autocorrelations (r1x, r1y) feeding N_eff will be computed on the interpolated series; linear interpolation over ≤6h gaps mechanically inflates r1 and biases N_eff downward. Acknowledge this bias or compute r1 on non-interpolated points only.

FR-003 and FR-010 require correlations and N_eff "on the full synchronized dataset / full continuous time series", and US-2's independent test says "Execute the correlation module on the full longitudinal dataset". The plan computes the primary results table only on the 1998–2017 training subset (Phase 2: "on the full 1998–2017 training series"). No plan element produces the full-dataset (1998–2020) 30-row table the spec mandates. Either add a full-period analysis step or the spec must be amended to define the training/validation split.

The plan's Project Structure lists contracts/dataset.schema.yaml and analysis_schema.schema.yaml, but the repo still contains a stale output.schema.yaml specifying "Thomson's MTM" EDF and "Holm-Bonferroni" p-values — methods with no FR backing (the plan itself reverted these as "un-spec'd elaborations"). This contract is a plan element with no FR/SC; delete it or regenerate it to match FR-004/FR-010 (plain Bonferroni, Pyper & Peterman N_eff).

FR-001 requires downloads "for any user-specified date range", but the plan hardcodes 1998-01-01–2020-12-31 with no CLI/config parameter for a user-specified range. Add a date-range argument to the fetch stage (or note the fixed range as a deliberate scope decision) so FR-001 is fully covered.

concerns.location: plan.md: Execution Plan Phase 0 / research.md Dataset Strategy
concerns.text: The plan names canonical sources (ACE SWEPAM/SWICS Level 2 via cdasws) but never names the actual CDAWeb dataset identifiers (e.g. AC_H0_SWE / AC_H2_SWE for SWEPAM, the SWICS Level 2 dataset id) that fetch_ace.py will request. The prior failure (T002 exit=2) was exactly a fetch-design problem; without the concrete dataset ids the re-planned fetch remains underspecified and risks a repeat failure. Add the CDAWeb dataset ids (and the specific NOAA SWPC / Kyoto WDC product file names) to the plan.

ACE SWICS He2+ abundance is known to have substantial data gaps and degraded coverage in the post-2011 era (SWICS instrument anomaly), which overlaps the entire 2018–2020 validation window. The plan's gap policy (interpolate ≤6 h, exclude >6 h) may leave helium_abundance largely excluded in the validation period, undermining the helium–Dst validation claim. The plan should acknowledge this coverage risk and state how the validation report will handle pairs with insufficient valid helium data.

Stale contract contradicts the re-plan. output.schema.yaml still specifies 'p_raw ... adjusted ... using Thomson's MTM' and 'p_holm_bonferroni' with field name 'composition_param', while plan.md Phase 2, research.md, data-model.md, and analysis_schema.schema.yaml all mandate Pyper & Peterman N_eff and plain Bonferroni with 'composition_parameter'/'p_bonferroni'. The plan's Project Structure lists only dataset.schema.yaml and analysis_schema.schema.yaml under contracts/, yet output.schema.yaml exists and could be exercised downstream, reintroducing the un-spec'd Holm/MTM methods the re-plan explicitly reverted. Delete or rewrite this contract to match.

Plan says synced.csv has 'the six required columns plus interpolated_flag' (i.e., 7 columns), while spec US-1's Independent Test says 'exactly five columns' but then lists six names (timestamp, proton_density, temperature, helium_abundance, Kp, Dst). The plan/data-model/contract are internally consistent (7 columns incl. flag); note the spec's own count discrepancy so a verifier doesn't fail the pipeline on the spec's 'five' wording.

The orphaned contract still specifies 'p_raw ... adjusted for effective degrees of freedom (EDF) using Thomson's MTM' and 'p_holm_bonferroni'. This contradicts the plan's reverted statistics (Pyper & Peterman N_eff + plain Bonferroni, FR-004/FR-010). A stale contract encoding the WRONG statistical method risks the implementer building against it. Delete or update output.schema.yaml to match analysis_schema.schema.yaml.

concerns.location: plan.md Phase 3 / spec US-3 acceptance scenario 2
concerns.text: The null-result report text asserts 'composition does not add predictive value beyond dynamic pressure' — but dynamic pressure is never measured or modeled anywhere in this pipeline. The analysis cannot support a comparison to an unmeasured variable; the report wording must be limited to what the 30 bivariate correlations can show (no pair exceeded |r|>0.5).

The plan applies the Pyper & Peterman N_eff (df = N_eff − 2) to BOTH Pearson and Spearman p-values without noting that the t-approximation with EDF is derived for Pearson r; for Spearman it is a common but approximate practice. Add one sentence acknowledging this approximation (or compute Spearman p via rank-transformed Pearson with the same EDF) so the choice is explicit.
